text:
maya: Hey team, just got a customer escalation — they say Console shows their route pinned to eu-west but their request IDs in our serving logs are all hitting us-central and latency spikes.
liam: Can you paste the customer request sample and timestamps? any API key or org id?
maya: Yep — customer sent this curl and timestamp. They repro consistently from their infra.
maya: ```curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-REDACTED\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-4o-mini\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate  # ts: 2024-06-06T15:12:33Z
``` 
maya: Console shows region badge: eu-west-1 for the route. Console request detail UI: \"served region: eu-west-1\" (screenshot attached in ticket). But our serving logs show requests routed to us-central-1 and we've got hop traces with LB info.
sophia: Confirming — I can repro from our side when forcing EU. UI claims eu-west, but trace contains x-redwood-pop: us-central-1 and extra ~120ms.
arthur: ops-bot picked up a routing change at 2024-06-06T15:10:50Z — auto-failover triggered due to degraded eu-west pool. LB seemed to fallback to us-central for capacity. The weird bit: console didn't flip status to \"failover\" for that route.
liam: That suggests mismatch between routing decisions in the control plane and what the Console surfaces. maya, can you share the request-id from the customer's header? we can correlate.
maya: Customer provided request-id: req_0a9f3c8e. Serving logs show: \"req_0a9f3c8e served_from: us-central-1, node: gpu-42, fallback_policy: allow_cross_region\".
arthur: Looking at control-plane events: at 15:10:49 we marked eu-west pool degraded but didn't emit the route-level telemetry event that the Console reads (bug in the telemetry fanout). LB did the fallback correctly, so real traffic went to us-central.
maya: Customer upset about latency and data residency. They want to know whether data was processed outside EU and how long before console will reflect fallback.
liam: Short answers: yes, fallback happened and traffic left EU. We need to provide remediation and timeline. maya — propose we offer a committed eu-only dedicated instance or immediate guidance: set route {\"strict_region\": true} to avoid cross-region fallbacks.
maya: I'll propose that. Also need an RCA for why Console didn't show the failover. arthur, ETA on fix for the telemetry fanout?
arthur: Root cause: a race in the fanout where the event stream to the console service can drop events when there are >500 concurrent pool state changes. Fix is queued; hotfix to make circuit breaker more lenient is deployable in ~2 hours, full fix in next sprint.
chris: Billing note: since fallback resulted in higher token egress cost we should flag this session for review and consider crediting overage if customer had region lock expectation. Who owns billing adjustment?
maya: I'll own the credit decision, liaise with chris.
liam: For immediate customer reply: acknowledge cross-region failover, explain cause (eu-west pool degradation + telemetry event drop), offer mitigation (strict_region flag or dedicated capacity) and timeline for console fix (~2 hours hotfix). Also include logs snippet and request id.
maya: Draft reply: \"We're very sorry — your requests were routed to us-central during an automated failover at 2024-06-06T15:10:50Z due to degraded eu-west capacity. We missed surfacing that failover in the Console due to a telemetry fanout race. We're rolling a hotfix to the Console within ~2h and can offer a region-exclusive Dedicated instance or immediate strict_region config to prevent cross-region fallback. We'll also review billing impact for the affected requests (request id req_0a9f3c8e).\" Thoughts?
arthur: Add that we rotated a short-term mitigation script to suppress further fanout drops; I'll attach the deploy id when done.
ops-bot: [alert] routing-fallback monitor triggered 12:15 UTC 2024-06-06; incident_id: rfb-20240606-1
sophia: Customer asked for forensic log lines proving where the request ran — I can export the serving node logs with req_0a9f3c8e if needed.
maya: Yes please include them in the ticket. chris: please review billing for potential credit.
liam: I'll follow up after the hotfix to confirm console events are flowing and close the loop with customer. Repro steps for internal: 1) degrade eu-west pool via chaos test 2) send requests with region preference but allow_cross_region 3) watch Console vs lb traces.
maya: Thanks, team. I'll update the customer and file a follow-up postmortem if needed. :thumbsup:
